sources.title: New York State Assembly, A6698 (2025-2026), reproducing General Construction Law § 24 as amended by chapter 249 of the laws of 2020 (its Asian Lunar New Year the bill's own proposal, not law; nysenate.gov's law pages answer this environment 403)
sources.said: § 24. Public holidays; half-holidays. The term public holiday includes the following days in each year: the first day of January, known as New Year's day; the third Monday of January, known as Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. day; the twelfth day of February, known as Lincoln's birthday; the third Monday in February, known as Washington's birthday; the last Monday in May, known as Memorial day; the second Sunday in June, known as Flag day (a Sunday, a day off already: not kept); the nineteenth day of June, known as Juneteenth; the fourth day of July, known as Independence day; the first Monday in September, known as Labor day; the second Monday in October, known as Columbus day; the eleventh day of November, known as Veterans' day; the fourth Thursday in November, known as Thanksgiving day; and the twenty-fifth day of December, known as Christmas day, and if any of such days except Flag day is Sunday, the next day thereafter; each general election day ...

sources.title: Ohio Revised Code, Section 124.19
sources.said: (A) State holidays shall be the first day of January, the third Monday in January, the third Monday in February, the day designated in the "Act of June 28, 1968," 82 Stat. 250, 5 U.S.C. 6103, as amended, for the commemoration of Memorial day, the nineteenth day of June, the fourth day of July, the first Monday in September, the second Monday in October, the eleventh day of November, the fourth Thursday in November, the twenty-fifth day of December, and any day appointed and recommended by the governor of this state or the president of the United States. (The federal holidays; none of Ohio's own.)

sources.title: Oklahoma Office of Management and Enterprise Services, Holidays (Executive Order 2025-14)

sources.title: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, Office of Administration, Administrative Circular 25-13 – Holidays - 2026 (August 19, 2025)
sources.said: Pursuant to Sections 221 and 709(e.1) of The Administrative Code of 1929, the Executive Board has determined that the administrative offices of State Government shall be closed on the following 2026 holidays: New Year's Day January 1; Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day January 19; Presidents' Day February 16; Memorial Day May 25; Juneteenth National Freedom Day June 19; Independence Day July 3; Labor Day September 7; Indigenous People’s Day October 12; Veterans Day November 11; Thanksgiving Day November 26; Day After Thanksgiving November 27; Christmas Day December 25. sources.title: Rhode Island General Laws § 25-1-1. General holidays enumerated
sources.said: The first day of January or, in the event that day is a Saturday or Sunday, then state employees will celebrate the holiday on the following Monday (as New Year’s Day), the third Monday of January ..., the third Monday of February (as Washington’s Birthday), the fourth day of May (as Rhode Island Independence Day), the last Monday of May (as Memorial Day), the nineteenth day of June or, in the event that day is a Saturday or Sunday, then state employees will celebrate the holiday on the following Monday (as Juneteenth National Freedom Day), the fourth day of July or ... the following Monday (as Independence Day), the second Monday of August (as Victory Day), the first Monday of September (as Labor Day), the second Monday of October (as Columbus Day), the eleventh day of November or ... the following Monday (as Veterans’ Day), the twenty-fifth day of December, or ... the following Monday (as Christmas Day) ..., the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November in each year in which a general election of state officers is held (as election day) ... shall be holidays.

sources.title: State of Rhode Island, Department of Administration, 2026 Payroll & Holiday Calendar
sources.said: 2026 State Holiday Celebrations: New Year’s Day Thursday, January 1; Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr Day Monday, January 19; Memorial Day Monday, May 25; Juneteenth Friday, June 19; Independence Day Saturday, July 4 (State Employees celebrate on Monday, July 6th); Victory Day Monday, August 10; Labor Day Monday, September 7; Columbus Day Monday, October 12; Election Day Tuesday, November 3; Veterans' Day Wednesday, November 11; Thanksgiving Day Thursday, November 26; Christmas Day Friday, December 25. (Washington's Birthday and Rhode Island Independence Day aren't state office closures: the 4 May isn't kept.)

sources.title: South Dakota Codified Law 1-5-1, Holidays enumerated
sources.said: The first day of every week, known as Sunday; the first day of January, commonly known as New Year's Day; the third Monday in January ... Martin Luther King, Jr. Day; the third Monday in February, the anniversary of the birthdays of Lincoln and Washington; the last Monday of May ... Memorial Day; the nineteenth day of June ... Juneteenth; the fourth day of July ... Independence Day; the first Monday in September ... Labor Day; the second Monday in October, commonly known as Native Americans' Day; the eleventh day of November, known as Veterans' Day; the fourth Thursday in November ... Thanksgiving Day; and the twenty-fifth day of December ... Christmas Day ... If the first day of January, the nineteenth day of June, the fourth day of July, the eleventh day of November, or the twenty-fifth day of December falls upon a Sunday, the Monday following is a legal holiday ...; and if any such day falls upon a Saturday, the preceding Friday is a legal holiday. (The federal days; none of South Dakota's own.)

sources.title: State of Tennessee, State Holidays
sources.said: Thursday, January 1, 2026, and Friday, January 2, 2026 – New Year's Day**; Monday, January 19 – Martin Luther King Jr. Day; Monday, February 16 – President's Day; Friday, April 3 – Good Friday; Monday, May 25 – Memorial Day; Friday, June 19 – Juneteenth; Friday, July 3 – Independence Day; Monday, September 7 – Labor Day; Wednesday, November 11 – Veterans Day; Thursday, November 26, and Friday, November 27 – Thanksgiving*; Thursday, December 24, and Friday, December 25 – Christmas**; Thursday, December 31, 2026, and Friday, January 1, 2027 – New Year's Day. * Following Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 4-4-105(a)(3), the Governor has designated that the Columbus Day holiday shall be substituted for the Friday after Thanksgiving. ** The Governor approved an added day of State office closure in addition to the official State holiday. When a holiday falls on Saturday, the Friday before the holiday is substituted. When the holiday falls on Sunday, the Monday following the holiday is substituted.

sources.title: Utah Code 63G-1-301, Legal holidays (the version superseded 1/1/2027, and the version amended by Chapter 124, 2026 General Session, effective 1/1/2027)
sources.said: (1) The following days are legal holidays in Utah: (a) (i) January 1, New Year's Day; (ii) July 4, Independence Day; (iii) July 24, Pioneer Day; (iv) November 11, Veterans Day; (v) December 25, Christmas; (b) (i) the third Monday of January ...; (iii) subject to Subsection (6), the Friday preceding Easter Sunday, Good Friday; ... (ix) June 19, Juneteenth National Freedom Day. (2) (a) If a day described in Subsection (1)(a) falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday is the legal holiday. (b) ... on a Sunday, the following Monday. (c) If June 19 falls on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday, the preceding Monday is the legal holiday. (d) If June 19 falls on Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday is the legal holiday. (6) A state employee ... will, for Good Friday, receive four hours of paid time off rather than the standard eight hours (half a day: not kept). From 1/1/2027, June 19 is among the days of (1)(a), moved only off a weekend.

sources.title: Code of Virginia § 2.2-3300. Legal holidays
sources.said: In each year, the following days are designated as legal holidays: January 1 — New Year's Day. The third Monday in January — Martin Luther King, Jr., Day. The third Monday in February — George Washington Day. The last Monday in May — Memorial Day. June 19 — Juneteenth. July 4 — Independence Day. The first Monday in September — Labor Day. The second Monday in October — Columbus Day and Yorktown Victory Day. The Tuesday following the first Monday in November — Election Day. November 11 — Veterans Day. The fourth Thursday in November and the Friday next following — Thanksgiving Day. December 25 — Christmas Day. Whenever any of such days falls on Saturday, the Friday next preceding such day, or whenever any of such days falls on Sunday, the Monday next following such day.

sources.said: Town Meeting Day: Tuesday, March 3 (2026); Tuesday, March 2 (2027).

sources.title: Revised Code of Washington 1.16.050, "Legal holidays" and "legislatively recognized days"
sources.said: (1) The following are state legal holidays: (a) Sunday; (b) The first day of January, commonly called New Year's Day; (c) The third Monday of January ... Martin Luther King, Jr.; (d) The third Monday of February, to be known as Presidents' Day; (e) The last Monday of May, commonly known as Memorial Day; (f) The nineteenth day of June, recognized as Juneteenth; (g) The fourth day of July; (h) The first Monday in September, to be known as Labor Day; (i) The eleventh day of November, to be known as Veterans Day; (j) The fourth Thursday in November, to be known as Thanksgiving Day; (k) The Friday immediately following the fourth Thursday in November, to be known as Native American Heritage Day; and (l) The twenty-fifth day of December, commonly called Christmas Day.

sources.title: Wisconsin Department of Administration, Division of Personnel Management, State Holidays (Wis. Stat. 230.35 (4); docs.legis.wisconsin.gov fails upstream from this environment)
sources.said: New Year's Day January 1; Martin Luther King, Jr.'s Birthday Third Monday in January; Memorial Day Last Monday in May; Independence Day July 4; Labor Day First Monday in September; Thanksgiving Day Fourth Thursday in November; Christmas Eve Day December 24; Christmas Day December 25; New Year's Eve Day December 31. (How a Christmas Eve or a New Year's Eve on a weekend is observed isn't given, so those aren't moved.)

sources.title: West Virginia Code §2-2-1, Legal holidays; official acts or court proceedings
sources.said: (a) The following days are legal holidays: (1) January 1 is "New Year's Day"; (2) The third Monday of January is "Martin Luther King's Birthday"; (3) The third Monday of February is "Presidents' Day"; (4) The last Monday in May is "Memorial Day"; (5) June 20 is "West Virginia Day"; (6) July 4 is "Independence Day"; (7) The first Monday of September is "Labor Day"; (8) The second Monday of October is "Columbus Day"; (9) November 11 is "Veterans' Day"; (10) The fourth Thursday of November is "Thanksgiving Day"; (11) The day after Thanksgiving Day is "Lincoln's Day"; (12) December 25 is "Christmas Day"; (13) Any day on which a general, primary or special election is held is a holiday throughout the state ...; (14) General election day on even years shall be designated Susan B. Anthony Day. (b) If a holiday ... falls on a Sunday, then the following Monday is the legal holiday. If ... on a Saturday, then the preceding Friday is the legal holiday: Provided, That this subsection shall not apply to subdivisions (13), (14), and (15). (The 2026 primary, 12 May, as the Legislature's calendar gives it; later primaries aren't dated yet.)

sources.title: West Virginia Legislature, Legislative Calendar - 2026
sources.said: 05/12/2026 - Primary Election Day; 11/03/2026 - General Election Day (Susan B. Anthony Day); 11/27/2026 Lincoln's Day.

sources.title: Wyoming Secretary of State, State Holidays
sources.said: New Year's Day January 1st*; Martin Luther King Jr. Day Third Monday in January; President's Day Third Monday in February; Memorial Day Last Monday in May; Independence Day July 4th*; Labor Day First Monday in September; Veterans Day November 11th*; Thanksgiving Fourth Thursday in November; Christmas December 25th*. If a holiday falls on a Saturday, the Office will be closed the day before (Friday). If the holiday falls on a Sunday, the Office will be closed the next day (Monday).
